item.title: Venezuela’s Reconciliation Talks Continued Progress Toward an Enduring Democracy
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Venezuela’s Reconciliation Talks Continued Progress Toward an Enduring Democracy 

Press Statement

November 24, 2026

The United States welcomes the conclusion of the latest round of political reconciliation talks between Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly, led by Dr. Dinorah Figuera, and the interim government.  This Venezuelan-led process continues to advance the institutional reforms and political freedoms necessary for free, fair, and credible elections following Operation Absolute Resolve.

The dialogue continues the progress to rebuild an independent Supreme Court.  The application period for the Supreme Court’s 32 new judges closed November 18 with over 1,300 applicants for these magistrate and other judiciary leadership positions.  The delegations also announced efforts to reform repressive laws, including reform of the Organized Crime and Terrorist Financing Law by the end of this year.  They agreed to conduct a consultation with all political organizations on reforming the Law on Political Parties, focusing on party status, registration updates and revalidation, and the creation of an ombudsman’s office to safeguard political participation.  The two sides also agreed to update and regularize specific broadcast media organizations’ concessions.

We encourage both sides to continue implementing their commitments, ensuring the participation of all political actors, and advancing toward credible elections.  We reiterate our call for the immediate release of all political prisoners.

The Trump Administration remains committed to supporting this Venezuelan-led process as part of President Trump and Secretary Rubio’s three-phase plan for stabilization, economic recovery, and political reconciliation leading to a peaceful democratic transition and an enduring republic.

item.title: Secretary Rubio’s Call with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Secretary Rubio’s Call with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud

Readout

November 24, 2026

Secretary Rubio spoke today with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud.  The Secretary condemned the Iran-backed Houthi terrorist attacks on Saudi civilian and energy infrastructure.  The Secretary and the Foreign Minister underscored the necessity of freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab Al-Mandeb.  The two discussed the need to end the war in Sudan, while Secretary Rubio also emphasized the importance of a humanitarian truce, durable peace, and transition to a civilian government. They also discussed the importance of Hizballah’s disarmament in Lebanon under the Trilateral Framework and a shared commitment to regional security and stability.

item.title: The United States Welcomes the Joint Bid by Chile and Belgium to Host the Secretariat of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

The United States Welcomes the Joint Bid by Chile and Belgium to Host the Secretariat of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement

Press Statement

November 24, 2026

The United States welcomes the joint offer by Chile and Belgium to host the Secretariat of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty.  Both countries have a strong record on ocean stewardship and transparency, and their partnership combines complementary expertise and expands diplomatic leadership in a way that reflects the Agreement’s broad membership.  The Trump Administration commends Chilean President Kast and Foreign Minister Pérez Mackenna and Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prevot for their contributions to this initiative.

The BBNJ Agreement can only succeed with a Secretariat that is independent, accountable to BBNJ Parties, and committed to protecting the integrity and security of the data and technology it manages.  If successful, this bid would allow the United States to engage more constructively in the BBNJ Agreement while we assess ratification.  We encourage all Parties to support the Chile-Belgium bid at the first Conference of the Parties in January 2027.

item.title: Joint Statement on the Eighth United States-Qatar Strategic Dialogue: An Enduring Strategic Partnership
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement on the Eighth United States-Qatar Strategic Dialogue: An Enduring Strategic Partnership

Media Note

November 23, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America and the State of Qatar.

Begin Text.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani convened the eighth U.S.-Qatar Strategic Dialogue on November 23, 2026, in Washington, D.C.  Senior officials from both governments also participated.  The two sides reaffirmed the enduring U.S.-Qatar strategic partnership under the leadership of President Donald J. Trump and His Highness the Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. 

As the United States and Qatar prepare to celebrate 55 years of diplomatic relations, the dialogue underscored their commitment to deepening cooperation and advancing global and regional priorities through diplomacy.  The United States and Qatar committed to expanding economic, commercial, and investment opportunities to enhance their mutual prosperity.  Discussions will continue into early 2027 on defense, security cooperation, counterterrorism, and law enforcement, and cultural ties.

Secretary Rubio reaffirmed the United States’ commitment to Qatar’s security. He underscored the importance of the defense partnership in strengthening joint capabilities and protecting shared interests. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to upholding freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. They stressed that safe and unimpeded passage through this vital waterway is essential to regional security, reliable energy supplies, and global economic stability.

On behalf of President Trump, Secretary Rubio expressed gratitude to His Highness the Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and the government of the State of Qatar for their leadership as a global mediator and close partner in advancing peace, stability, and security worldwide. Prime Minister Al Thani commended President Trump’s leadership in pursuing agreements to resolve regional conflicts and underscored the central role of U.S. diplomatic engagement in creating the conditions for lasting peace.

Prime Minister Al-Thani also congratulated the United States on its successful co-hosting of the FIFA World Cup 2026.

Global and Regional Cooperation

Secretary of State Rubio affirmed the U.S.-Qatar partnership as a model of peace through strength and a force for stability amid regional and global challenges.  U.S. and Qatari officials discussed shared policy priorities in Gaza, Iran, Syria, Lebanon, Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Sahel, Rwanda, Somalia, Bolivia, and Haiti.   Together, the United States and Qatar are shaping a future grounded in peace, where terrorism has no place.

Secretary Rubio expressed appreciation for Qatar’s continued support of Haiti, including a $30 million pledge to the UN Trust Fund for the Gang Suppression Force.

Economic Affairs and Investments

The United States and Qatar highlighted their strong economic partnership, which continues to grow both economies, create jobs, and advance cooperation in energy and emerging technology.  Building on the more than $240 billion in economic deals announced during President Trump’s May 2025 visit to Qatar, both sides discussed expanding opportunities for U.S. companies in Qatar and promoting Qatari investment in the United States, including through the Qatar Investment Authority.  The United States highlighted ongoing efforts to promote a welcoming investment climate through the U.S. Investment Accelerator and SelectUSA, while Qatar underscored the importance of U.S. partnerships to its economic diversification.

The United States welcomed Qatar’s signing of the Pax Silica Declaration and the two countries’ growing cooperation on super intelligence, high-performance computing, trusted digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and other advanced technologies, as well as secure supply chains for energy and critical minerals.  Both sides emphasized their shared interest in promoting global energy abundance and resilience, including through the Golden Pass LNG project.

The United States and Qatar signed a Critical Minerals Framework to deepen collaboration on and align national strategies for diversifying critical mineral supply chains and strengthening global supply chain resilience.

Defense and Security Cooperation

The United States and Qatar pledged to strengthen their longstanding defense and security partnership through defense sales, joint exercises, and intelligence sharing efforts, while also pursuing new opportunities in critical minerals, regional sustainment, and industrial cooperation. Building on the September 2026 U.S.–Qatar Military Consultative Commission, both sides discussed ways to enhance Qatar’s integrated air and missile defense capabilities to better protect its territory and critical infrastructure.

Both sides reviewed progress under the $38 billion U.S.-Qatar Statement of Intent on defense cooperation and discussed potential investments in critical munitions and platforms that support interoperability between U.S. and Qatari forces. They highlighted opportunities to strengthen Qatar’s defenses and expand U.S. defense manufacturing through investment in missile defense and counter-unmanned aircraft capabilities. 

Counterterrorism and Law Enforcement

The United States and Qatar stressed the importance of working together to counter terrorism, terrorist financing, and transnational organized crime. Both sides highlighted close interagency and law enforcement cooperation between the U.S. Departments of Homeland Security, Treasury, Justice, and State and Qatar’s Ministry of Interior, Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya), State Security Bureau, and Public Prosecution Office.  They welcomed ongoing cooperation on international prisoner transfers and efforts to disrupt money laundering networks.  The two sides also reviewed joint efforts to counter ISIS, including through the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS.

The two governments discussed expanding information sharing to strengthen customs and border security cooperation and explored ways to build both countries’ capacity to counter transnational threats. Underscoring the close partnership between the FBI and Qatar’s Ministry of Interior, both sides welcomed the new joint training, collaboration, and investment at the FBI’s Redstone Arsenal Headquarters. 

Education and Culture

Qatar and the United States underscored the strength of their enduring partnership in education, culture, and sports. The two countries recognized the value of their decades-long educational ties and Qatar’s role in strengthening the presence of leading U.S. academic institutions in the region, particularly through Education City.

Both sides emphasized the importance of expanding partnerships between U.S. higher education institutions, Qatari universities, and the private sector to drive research, innovation, and workforce development that benefit both countries and future generations.

End Text.

item.title: Severing the Financial Lifelines of Iran’s Shadow Banking Network
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Severing the Financial Lifelines of Iran’s Shadow Banking Network

Press Statement

November 23, 2026

Today, the United States is taking action against more than two dozen exchange houses, front companies, and individuals in Iran, the United Arab Emirates, Türkiye, and Hong Kong that support Iran’s shadow banking system. This action is part of Operation Economic Outcast, the whole-of-government campaign to sever the economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime.

The Iranian regime uses its shadow banking networks to seek to fund the purchase of weapons and support terrorist proxies across the Middle East. The regime continues to prioritize funding terror and destabilization abroad while the Iranian people pay the price at home.

These networks use thousands of shell and front companies in multiple jurisdictions to move significant funds for Iranian state-linked customers.

The United States will continue to use every diplomatic and economic tool available to deny the Iranian regime the resources it needs to threaten our forces, our partners, and global security.

Today’s action is being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets certain sectors of the Iranian economy, including Iran’s financial sector, E.O. 13224, as amended, a counterterrorism designation authority, and E.O. 13871, which targets persons operating in various sectors of Iran’s metals industry. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s Press Releases.

item.title: First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together Gathers European Leaders for Summit Hosted by Poland’s First Lady Marta Nawrocka
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together Gathers European Leaders for Summit Hosted by Poland’s First Lady Marta Nawrocka

Media Note

November 23, 2026

On November 18-19, First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together initiative brought leaders together in Warsaw for the “Their Future. Our Responsibility.” Summit, hosted by Poland’s First Lady, Mrs. Marta Nawrocka.  The summit advanced Mrs. Trump’s global leadership, bringing together regional first spouses to address the shared responsibility for the safety, well-being, and future of children and young people in an increasingly digital world. First spouses from Poland, Lithuania, Romania, Slovenia, and Ukraine participated in the summit.

First Lady Melania Trump inspired the member nations present at the Fostering the Future Together European Summit via video, stating that, “Throughout history, Europe has been at the forefront of technological innovation and education from the rise of the Universities at Oxford, Paris, Cambridge, and Krakow which helped shape the global higher education system to the Enlightenment and the Industrial Revolution. Today, I challenge every nation to build on Europe’s rich legacy, your legacy, and advance Fostering the Future Together’s mission.”

On behalf of First Lady Melania Trump, Special Envoy Charity Wallace joined the first spouses in addressing an audience of policymakers and private sector partners about the unique challenges and opportunities that education and technology present for children in the region. Together, they explored how to advance shared goals and use their platforms to educate and empower future generations through technology and emphasized their deep commitment to the Fostering the Future Together initiative. They applauded Mrs. Trump’s leadership, acknowledging her impact in spearheading these efforts.

Through Fostering the Future Together, Mrs. Trump and her coalition partners are opening doors to education and technology, keeping children safe online, and preparing young people for the age of Super Intelligence (SI).

First Lady Melania Trump’s message to the gathering may be viewed here.

item.title: Lebanon National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Lebanon National Day

Press Statement

November 22, 2026

The United States of America extends its congratulations to the people of Lebanon on the 83rd anniversary of their independence. The Lebanese people have shown extraordinary talent and resilience, both at home and across their global diaspora. On this occasion, the United States reaffirms its support for a fully sovereign Lebanon, at peace with its neighbors and accountable only to its own citizens. We will continue to stand with the Lebanese people and the Lebanese state, and look forward to growing the partnership between our two nations.

item.title: Sanctioning Iranian Regime Insiders Who Profit from Stolen Oil Wealth
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Sanctioning Iranian Regime Insiders Who Profit from Stolen Oil Wealth

Press Statement

November 20, 2026

Today, the United States took action against four corrupt Iranian regime insiders who illicitly sell oil to help fund the regime’s military and its support for terrorism. Those designated include a former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) intelligence officer and the son of the head of Mahan Air, an airline the regime uses to move weapons and fighters for the IRGC-Qods Force.

Today’s action is part of Operation Economic Outcast, a whole-of-government campaign to cut off illicit money flows that sustain the Iranian regime. The United States will continue working to deny Tehran the revenue it uses to destabilize the region, threaten our partners, and pursue its dangerous ambitions.

Today’s designations are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum, petrochemical, and aviation sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy, and E.O. 13224, as amended, a counterterrorism authority. For more information, please see Treasury’s Press Release.

item.title: Joint Statement on the Sixth U.S.-Germany Joint Committee Meeting on Science and Technology Cooperation
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement on the Sixth U.S.-Germany Joint Committee Meeting on Science and Technology Cooperation

Media Note

November 20, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America and Germany.

Begin Text

The United States hosted the Federal Republic of Germany in Washington, DC, on November 19-20, 2026, for the 6th U.S.-Germany Joint Committee Meeting (JCM) on Science and Technology Cooperation. The State Department’s Assistant Secretary for European and Eurasian Affairs, Brendan Hanrahan, co-chaired the meeting with Germany’s Dr. Effrosyni Chelioti, Director General for Strategies and Policy Issues and International Affairs and Europe at the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space.

The delegations used this JCM to deepen their cooperation in robotics, fusion energy, biotechnology, and critical minerals recovery. The delegations decided to promote joint research, agency-to-agency partnerships, shared technical standards where appropriate, and public-private collaboration to accelerate the path from scientific discovery to commercial application.

Both delegations reaffirmed the importance of securing the shared research ecosystem, determining to strengthen information-sharing and risk-analysis cooperation via Germany’s National Research Security Platform. The two countries underscored that protecting critical and emerging technologies is essential to safeguarding the integrity of the bilateral research relationship.

Both countries reaffirmed their commitment to a partnership that pairs German research, engineering, and manufacturing excellence with American research and commercialization strength, powering innovation that is mutually beneficial.

End Text
item.content:encoded:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement on the Sixth U.S.-Germany Joint Committee Meeting on Science and Technology Cooperation

Media Note

November 20, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America and Germany.

Begin Text

The United States hosted the Federal Republic of Germany in Washington, DC, on November 19-20, 2026, for the 6th U.S.-Germany Joint Committee Meeting (JCM) on Science and Technology Cooperation. The State Department’s Assistant Secretary for European and Eurasian Affairs, Brendan Hanrahan, co-chaired the meeting with Germany’s Dr. Effrosyni Chelioti, Director General for Strategies and Policy Issues and International Affairs and Europe at the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space.

The delegations used this JCM to deepen their cooperation in robotics, fusion energy, biotechnology, and critical minerals recovery. The delegations decided to promote joint research, agency-to-agency partnerships, shared technical standards where appropriate, and public-private collaboration to accelerate the path from scientific discovery to commercial application.

Both delegations reaffirmed the importance of securing the shared research ecosystem, determining to strengthen information-sharing and risk-analysis cooperation via Germany’s National Research Security Platform. The two countries underscored that protecting critical and emerging technologies is essential to safeguarding the integrity of the bilateral research relationship.

Both countries reaffirmed their commitment to a partnership that pairs German research, engineering, and manufacturing excellence with American research and commercialization strength, powering innovation that is mutually beneficial.
